blocks.html: Earthquake hazard is classified as very low for Curitiba on ThinkHazard (GFDRR / World Bank tool, using GEM data): less than a 2% chance of potentially damaging shaking in 50 years. That is a regional model, not a building-by-building assessment.

items.title: Earthquakes
items.html: Unlike Bucaramanga, Curitiba is not in a high-seismic setting on the source reviewed. The 2010+ tower rule is still applied here as your standing criteria, not because of a local seismic code equivalent to Colombia’s NSR-10. No municipal post-quake inspection protocol was researched, because no recent damaging quake in Curitiba was found in this pass.

items.title: Flooding / alagamentos
items.html: This is the clearer natural hazard. The City of Curitiba (May 13, 2026) called the Córrego do Bigorrilho basin historically vulnerable to flooding because of soil sealing. The stream rises near Padre Agostinho / Padre Anchieta in Mercês, runs toward the Center (including Rua Professor Fernando Moreira / Rua dos Chorões), and joins the Rio Ivo near Praça Osório. The city finished a channel cleaning there in May 2026 and published a bid for drainage studies (proposal opening July 7, 2026). A 2020 municipal climate-risk study also flagged future alagamento risk in several central neighborhoods, including Batel, Mercês, Cabral, Ahú, Centro Cívico, Alto da Glória and Juvevê (maps are for 2030–2100 scenarios, not a street-level guarantee). A PUCPR/IPPUC project, reported by Plural (updated Jan 3, 2026) and Tribuna, found media reports of flooding concentrated in Centro, Rebouças, Água Verde, Portão, Lindóia and Capão Raso.

items.title: Cold winters
items.html: Curitiba is one of Brazil’s colder state capitals. INMET’s June 2025 climate bulletin for station A807 recorded a monthly mean of 15.3°C (1.9°C below the 1991–2020 normal of 17.2°C), a mean minimum of 10.9°C (normal 13.6°C), and a lowest temperature of −0.3°C on June 25, 2025. Ask about heating, sun exposure, window seals and winter damp/mold before signing — that checklist itself is general info.

items.title: Crime — what is sourced
items.html: Tribuna do Paraná (June 11, 2026), citing Sesp-PR figures for the first quarter of 2026, listed the 10 neighborhoods with the most police reports: Centro (4,191), CIC (2,656), Sítio Cercado (1,752), Cajuru (1,584), Boqueirão (1,547), Água Verde (1,453), Tatuquara (1,176), Uberaba (1,163), Portão (1,097) and Pinheirinho (982). The article says Centro, Água Verde and Portão are driven mainly by thefts and fraud (estelionato), while more violent deaths were concentrated in CIC, Sítio Cercado and Cajuru. Batel, Bigorrilho, Cabral, Ahú, Juvevê, Mercês, Cristo Rei, Alto da Glória, Ecoville/Mossunguê, Centro Cívico and Bacacheri were not in that top 10. That is not a finding that those areas are “safe” — only that they were not among the ten highest-volume neighborhoods in that ranking. High-circulation commercial streets can still have theft. No official per-neighborhood rates (adjusted for population or visitors) were found in this pass.

blocks.title: Renter checklist
items: Ask for the building’s ano de construção or the habite-se / construction documents, especially for any tower.
Ask whether the unit or the street has flooded, and check the building’s relation to the Córrego do Bigorrilho or other channels if you are in Mercês, Bigorrilho, Batel or nearby.
In winter, look at sun exposure, window seals, heating (split or other), and signs of damp or mold.
Walk the block at night as well as by day; prefer buildings with a doorman if that matters to you.
Get condomínio, IPTU, water, gas, electricity and any fundo de conservação / inspection fees in writing.
Get a written inventory (vistoria) of the furniture before you move in.

sections.title: Cost of living & renting as a foreigner

items.title: Rental guarantees (Lei do Inquilinato)
items.html: Lei nº 8.245/1991, art. 37, lets a landlord require one of four guarantees: caução (deposit), fiança (a fiador / co-signer), seguro de fiança locatícia (seguro-fiança), or assignment of investment-fund shares. Stacking more than one in the same contract is void. A cash caução may not exceed three months’ rent and must be placed in a savings account, with the yield going to the tenant (art. 38, § 2º). In practice many agencies still prefer a Brazilian fiador or an insurer’s approval for seguro-fiança — that practice is not spelled out in the statute.

items.title: CPF
items.html: The Tenancy Law does not itself require a CPF to sign a lease, but banks, insurers and most agencies do. Receita Federal / gov.br (page last modified Dec 15, 2025) says foreigners living abroad must apply for a CPF in person at a Brazilian consular post, booked through e-Consular. The service is free. Get this before you start formal lease applications if you can.

items.title: Visitor visa (VIVIS / e-Visa) — US citizens
items.html: Since April 10, 2025, US citizens need a visitor visa to enter Brazil for tourism or business. The e-Visa (VIVIS) is applied for online through VFS Global. The Brazilian Embassy in Canberra page (updated Oct 29, 2026) says stays are up to 90 days, no more than 180 days per year, the visa is valid for up to 5 years with multiple entries, and the fee is US$ 80.90. Extensions, once you are in Brazil, are at the discretion of immigration authorities. A 90-day visitor stay is a poor match for a standard 12-month unfurnished lease; furnished monthly rentals are the usual bridge. Confirm current rules on the official sites before you travel — they can change.

items.title: Longer stays — VITEM XIV / digital nomad
items.html: For a stay meant as residence, look at a temporary visa. The Ministry of Justice page reproduces Resolução Normativa CNIG nº 45/2021: a “nômade digital” works remotely for a foreign employer, must show at least US$ 1,500/month or US$ 18,000 available, and the initial residence period is up to one year, renewable for an equal period. The Brazilian Consulate in Boston (updated Nov 19, 2024) lists the same income tests, plus a retirement/pensioner path at US$ 2,000/month, and says the digital-nomad fee for US citizens has been US$ 290 since Aug 15, 2023. You may also need to deal with Federal Police registration and a CRNM once in Brazil — check the latest consular instructions. This is not legal advice.

Up Garden (delivered Nov 2025) comes from a sale ad for the same address; a 2023 advertorial had planned August 2025. Residence Versailles is estimated ~1995 from the condominium CNPJ opening date.
Listings 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12 have no verified year. Listing 8 is a pre-2010 tower and does not meet the 2010+ rule.
Building height is unconfirmed or only inferred (elevators, amenities) for listings 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12. Listings 10 and 11 are marked “height unknown.”
Furnished is “not stated” for listing 12. Listing 3’s ad says fully furnished but also lists “Semi Mobiliado.”

Several advertised rents are net of a punctuality discount (listings 2 and 6 bill a higher first month). Listing 10 showed two different headline prices — confirm. Listing 1 has slightly different long-stay package prices on the same page.
No furnished 2-bedroom house or confirmed ≤2-story building was found in the named neighborhoods on this pass.

No verified furnished 2BR listing with a stable URL was captured in Cabral, Ahú, Juvevê, Mercês, Cristo Rei, Centro Cívico or Bacacheri. QuintoAndar search pages showed some nearby items (including a furnished 2BR in Ahú) without a durable listing URL in the extracted page.

ZAP Imóveis, Viva Real, OLX, Imovelweb and Airbnb monthly were searched; they did not yield usable individual listing pages with complete prices and years in this pass (often JavaScript-heavy or without a stable URL). Mercado-style Facebook groups were not checked.

USD amounts use the official PTAX venda of 5.8573 BRL per USD for Nov 24, 2026, the latest closing rate published when this was researched in the early hours of Nov 25, 2026 (America/New_York). The Nov 25 PTAX had not been published yet.
QuintoAndar “valor médio” figures mix furnished and unfurnished 2BR asking rents and can be skewed by a few expensive units (notably Mercês and one of the Batel averages).
Neighborhood safety comments use a citywide count of police reports, not crime rates. Absence from the top 10 is not a safety rating.
